What is in our bulk glutathione cream?

The cream in our bulk tubs is the same formula we fill into the Glutathione Cream 30 g jar. Here is what each ingredient does, in cosmetic terms:

  • Glutathione: an antioxidant that helps skin look fresher and more radiant with regular use.
  • Vitamin C: another antioxidant, popular for a brighter-looking finish.
  • Kojic acid: helps reduce the look of dark spots and uneven tone over several weeks.
  • Vitamin B3 (niacinamide): helps skin look smoother and more even.
  • Aloe vera: soothing and helps skin feel moisturised.

It is a cosmetic cream. It helps skin look brighter and more even over time, but it does not change natural skin colour, and your customers should know that. For a plain-language explainer you can share, see glutathione cream benefits and how to use glutathione cream.

What decides the price per kg?

We do not publish a fixed rate, because the price of glutathione cream in kg depends on three things:

  1. The cream: glutathione cream has more active ingredients than our simple avocado cream, so it costs more per kilo.
  2. The quantity: larger orders get a lower rate per kg.
  3. The packing: loose cream in bulk tubs costs less than cream filled into finished jars.

Using bulk glutathione cream safely with clients

  • Patch test on each new client, on the jawline or behind the ear, before a full facial.
  • Avoid using it straight after a strong peel, waxing or threading on the same area.
  • Remind clients to wear sunscreen every morning, because the cream contains kojic acid and vitamin C.
  • Explain realistic timelines: skin renews roughly every 4–6 weeks, and a more even look usually takes 8–12 weeks of regular use. Our guide on how long glutathione cream takes to work covers this.
  • Pregnant clients, or clients with melasma, rashes or painful acne, should see a dermatologist first.

Storage and repacking

Keep the tub closed in a cool, dry place away from sunlight. Use a clean, dry spatula every time and never return unused cream to the tub. Check the batch number and use-before date on each container. If you repack or sell under your own brand, the labelling and licence rules for cosmetics in India apply to your business, so check them before you sell.
